featured_reviews.name: nikita zade
featured_reviews.review_text:
My father passed away on 18th April, and despite several follow-ups, this hospital has still not submitted the required documents to the BMC for the death certificate process. At a time when a grieving family is already under immense emotional stress, the complete lack of urgency, empathy, and basic decency shown by the staff has been deeply disturbing.

What made the experience even worse was the sheer negligence of the staff. On the very next day after the passing, we had to revisit the hospital because the team had forgotten to take a required signature. Such basic procedural lapses during such a sensitive time are simply unacceptable.

The entire case was handled in an extremely disappointing manner, and the communication with the family of a deceased patient was insensitive and unprofessional throughout. Instead of supporting us during an already painful situation, the hospital added unnecessary emotional trauma, frustration, and repeated inconvenience.

I strongly urge people to think twice before opting for services here. Compassion, accountability, professionalism, and timely administrative support are the bare minimum expected from any hospital, and unfortunately, we experienced none of these.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Namaste Nikita,
We are extremely sorry to learn of your loss and extend our condolences to the departed soul. We request you to please share your contact details and patient’s UHID by writing to us at feedback@hcgel.com. I recently consulted Dr. Ronak Jariwala at the Powai Hospital OPD for a persistent throat issue, and I cannot recommend him highly enough.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Powai Hospital for eye checkups for myself, my mother, and my wife, and we had a truly reassuring experience with Dr. Ashish Shinde and Dr. Himalee Bhadange Shinde. They are a husband and wife team who see patients in different time slots, which made it convenient for all of us to schedule our visits.

I consulted Dr. Ashish Shinde for a routine eye checkup and really appreciated how thorough and informative he was. He took the time to explain everything clearly and made the entire process feel calm and comfortable. My mother also saw him for a specific issue, and we were relieved that her concern was properly diagnosed and effectively treated.

My wife visited Dr. Himalee Bhadange Shinde, and her experience was equally positive. She had been dealing with an eye issue for some time, and Dr Himalee handled it with great care and attention. She explained the condition in a way that was easy to understand and provided the right treatment, which made a noticeable difference.

Overall, both doctors are highly professional, patient, and genuinely caring. It is rare to find such a combination of expertise and warmth. We all left feeling confident and well taken care of, and I would definitely recommend them to anyone looking for reliable eye care.

featured_reviews.name: Priyansh Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dr. Aniket Mishra, a general physician, for my wife’s health concerns. Unfortunately, the experience was disappointing. Without conducting any proper check-up other than blood pressure, or reviewing blood reports, he immediately suggested hospital admission and IV saline treatment.
When I declined admission, he prescribed 4–5 medications. I specifically requested that he prescribe medicines that are commonly available at regular pharmacies, rather than only at the hospital’s in-house medical store. His response was dismissive, stating that if chemists don’t recognize these medicines, they shouldn’t be working there.
However, when I went to my regular pharmacy, I was informed that the prescribed medicines are typically only available at the hospital’s own store and not elsewhere.
This is not the first time I’ve faced this issue with the same doctor, which is why I had made the request in advance. This kind of practice feels inconvenient and raises concerns about transparency and patient-first care.

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Av
featured_reviews.review_text:
I was admitted to Sapna Hospital for malaria and stayed for 4 days.
It was extremely concerning to see mosquito issues inside the ward while being treated for a mosquito-borne illness. A repellent machine was only provided after repeated complaints.
Hygiene standards were disappointing. I noticed what appeared to be blood stains in saline lines, a dustbin near my bed containing vomit that was not cleared promptly, and an ice pad provided to me that had visible hair on it. Used gloves were also left openly near patient beds instead of being disposed of immediately and bed bugs.
These are basic infection-control practices that should be strictly maintained in any hospital.
Staff behavior at times felt indifferent, and response seemed noticeably quicker when services involved billing.
For a bill of approximately ₹30,000 in just 3 days, I expected a much higher standard of cleanliness, monitoring, and patient care.
I hope the management takes this feedback seriously and improves hygiene control and patient handling to ensure patient safety.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Today I came to Mumbai and it reminded me of this hospital. In 2024 I admitted my sister here but forgot to write the review. So here it is.

It was early morning and my sister had sudden pain in her stomach. Looking at the pain I was quite evident that it was due to stone. As we were near to Parakh hospital we reached there. As per doctor's advice ultrasound was done and as I thought it was due to stone only. We requested doctor to provide some medicine for getting relief from pain so that we can go back to Gwalior and we will take further treatment there as it is our hometown. But he insisted for getting admitted. Considering the pain we decided for getting admitted. They kept giving my sister injections and medicines for holding the pain. Also ran some other tests. After 24 hours they started insisting for surgery. We finally decided to get discharged from the hospital. The total expense that we had to pay for this 1 day was 30000/-
Worse part was that immediately after the discharge the pain returned and my sister was still in the same situation as 1 day before.
At last I went to a medical store nearby and told him about the pain. The medical store guy gave just 1 pill and with that medicine the entire pain vanished and my sister reached back Gwalior via train without any pain.
In Gwalior she took homeopathy medicine treatment and in six months all the stones are gone without any surgery.

So I'm not sure about how this hospital is at present but in October 2024 they literally looted us in just a single day. So beware.
